title: The Shudder at 45
complaintTemplate: CUST STATES: around 40-50 mph on light throttle it feels like driving over rumble strips for a few seconds. Goes away if I get on it or if I drop a gear. Smooth everywhere else. Another shop said the transmission is going and quoted a rebuild.

faultSeeds.internalNote: The classic. Torque-converter clutch shudder on apply — degraded fluid, friction material no longer grabbing cleanly. Tracks converter lockup, not road speed. Correct fix: fluid exchange with the correct spec fluid plus a relearn — NOT a rebuild. Confirming test: act_roadtest_log (TCC slip oscillating while the shudder is felt).

activeFaults.label: torque-converter clutch shuddering on apply from degraded fluid

resultOverrides.act_roadtest_log: Between 43 and 48 mph on light throttle, TCC slip speed oscillates a few hundred RPM in time with the shudder, then settles when it fully locks. Misfire counters stay at zero throughout.
resultOverrides.act_speed_vs_rpm: Holding the same road speed in a lower gear, the converter unlocks and the shudder disappears entirely. It follows converter lockup, not road speed.
resultOverrides.act_misfire_data: No misfire counts on any cylinder, loaded or unloaded.
resultOverrides.act_fluid_check: The fluid is dark and smells scorched, and there's no record of it ever being serviced.
resultOverrides.act_tire_balance: All four wheels balance within spec. The shudder is completely unchanged afterward.

faultSeeds.internalNote: The engine problem wearing a transmission costume. A coil breaking down under load misfires only when cylinder pressure is high — light-throttle cruise at 45 is exactly that load. Feels identical to a shudder from the driver's seat. Correct fix: coil (and plug) on the affected cylinder. Confirming test: act_misfire_data.

activeFaults.label: cylinder 5 coil breaking down under load

resultOverrides.act_roadtest_log: The shudder is there at 45 on light throttle, but TCC slip holds within a few RPM the whole time. Something else is shaking it.
resultOverrides.act_speed_vs_rpm: The shudder follows engine load and RPM — it shows up in any gear that puts the engine under the same load, at whatever road speed that happens to be.
resultOverrides.act_misfire_data: Cylinder 5 accumulates misfire counts every time it's under load at cruise, with a pending misfire code stored for that cylinder. The counts stop at idle.
resultOverrides.act_fluid_check: The transmission fluid is clean, at the correct level, with no burnt smell.
resultOverrides.act_tire_balance: All four balance within spec and nothing changes.

faultSeeds.internalNote: The one that isn't the powertrain at all. A worn driveshaft center-support bearing puts in a vibration tied purely to road speed — same at 45 mph in any gear. Correct fix: center-support bearing / driveshaft service. Confirming test: act_speed_vs_rpm (identical at the same road speed regardless of gear).

resultOverrides.act_roadtest_log: The vibration is present at 45 mph, but TCC slip is steady and no misfire counts accumulate. The scan data looks unremarkable.
resultOverrides.act_speed_vs_rpm: At the same road speed in a different gear the vibration is exactly the same. Change the road speed and it changes. It tracks road speed, not engine RPM.
resultOverrides.act_misfire_data: No misfire counts on any cylinder.
resultOverrides.act_fluid_check: Transmission fluid looks and smells normal.
resultOverrides.act_tire_balance: All four balance within spec, and the vibration is unchanged.

nodes.prompt: A rumble-strip shudder in a narrow speed band on light throttle, and somebody has already quoted a transmission rebuild. Where do you start?

options.label: Road-test it with the scan tool logging TCC slip and misfire counts
Road-test it to isolate whether it follows RPM or road speed
Pull it in and start a full workup
Shudder at cruise on a truck this age — quote the rebuild

nodes.prompt: Truck's yours. What's your move?

options.label: Road-test with scan data on TCC slip and misfire counters
Road-test holding speed across gears to isolate RPM vs road speed
Check misfire counters cylinder by cylinder under load
Inspect the transmission fluid condition and level
Balance and rotate the tires and see if it goes away
I'm ready to commit to a root cause

nodes.prompt: A torque-converter clutch shudder is —
nodes.explanation: The TCC is a friction clutch locking the engine directly to the transmission. When the fluid or friction material degrades, it grabs and slips repeatedly on apply instead of locking cleanly — felt as a rumble-strip shudder in the lockup speed band.

options.label: the clutch slipping and grabbing as it tries to lock up
the converter stator freewheeling at highway speed
the planetary gearset skipping under light throttle
the fluid pump cavitating because the level is low

nodes.prompt: You road-test it with the scan tool logging TCC slip speed, misfire counters, engine load and vehicle speed, and reproduce the shudder in its speed band.

options.label: Log it and isolate RPM versus road speed
Log it and check the fluid condition
Log it and commit

nodes.prompt: It shudders at 45 mph. Which move tells you whether it follows engine speed or road speed?
nodes.explanation: Same road speed, different gear: road speed is held constant while RPM and lockup state change. If the shudder moves with the gear it's engine or converter related; if it stays put at that road speed, it's in the driveline or wheels.

options.label: Balance the tires and then road-test it again
Watch whether it changes when the A/C compressor cycles on
Check the driveline and carrier bearing for play up on a lift
Hold the same speed in a lower gear — RPM changes, speed doesn't

nodes.prompt: You hold the same road speed in different gears, then vary road speed at the same RPM, feeling for what the shudder actually tracks.

options.label: Log it and road-test with scan data
Log it and check misfire counters under load
Log it and commit

nodes.prompt: Why might a failing coil misfire only under load?
nodes.explanation: Higher cylinder pressure raises the voltage needed to jump the plug gap. A weak coil makes enough voltage at idle and runs out of margin under load — which is why it only misfires where the engine is working.

options.label: Cold injectors flow less fuel at higher engine speed
Exhaust backpressure rises and quenches the spark
Cylinder pressure rises, so the spark needs more voltage
The knock sensor retards timing until the misfire clears

nodes.prompt: You watch misfire counters cylinder by cylinder while holding the truck at cruise load, and check for pending codes afterward.

options.label: Log it and road-test with full scan data
Log it and commit

nodes.prompt: You check the transmission fluid level, colour and smell, and look for any service history on it.

options.label: Log it and road-test with scan data
Log it and commit

nodes.prompt: You pull all four wheels, balance them, rotate them and road-test it again.
nodes.continueLabel: That didn't touch it — back to the workup

nodes.prompt: Commit to a specific root cause. There's a transmission rebuild quote sitting on the counter next to yours.

options.label: It's TCC shudder — correct-spec fluid exchange and relearn
It's a misfire under load — coil and plug on that cylinder
It's the driveshaft center-support bearing — replace it
The other shop's right — sell the transmission rebuild
Couldn't duplicate anything conclusive — send it back out

nodes.prompt: You do a full fluid exchange with the correct-spec fluid and run the TCC adaptive relearn.
You replace the coil and plug on the affected cylinder and clear the misfire history.
You replace the driveshaft center-support bearing and re-index the shaft on reassembly.
You send it out for a transmission rebuild — several thousand dollars and most of a week. It comes back with a reman converter in it.
nodes.continueLabel: Get it back from the builder

nodes.prompt: You write 'could not duplicate' on the ticket and hand back the keys.
Before it goes back — how do you confirm the shudder is actually gone?

options.label: Road-test the same speed band and load that produced it
It's smooth pulling out of the bay — release it

nodes.prompt: You road-test it through the exact speed band and throttle position the customer described, with the scan tool still logging.
It runs through the whole 40-50 band on light throttle dead smooth, in every gear, repeatedly. You proved what it tracked before you spent the customer's money.
It's back on the schedule with the same rumble at the same speed. Whatever was actually shaking it is still there.
